title: A novel device for detecting anaerobic threshold using sweat lactate during exercise
population: 23 healthy adults and 42 patients with cardiovascular disease
n_primary_analysis: Responsive/analyzable subsets; 23 CVD sensor responders and 13 CVD with blood lactate
sensor_site: upper arm in healthy participants; forehead in CVD
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: blood LT1 and ventilatory threshold VT1
key_result: sLT-bLT r=0.92; sLT-VT1 r=0.71; mean differences -4.5 W and 2.5 W; low sweating caused nonresponse
fatigue_relevance: indirect; establishes threshold method used by later fatigue studies
main_limitations: small observational study; incomplete analyzability; no sweat-rate measurement; no LOx-free control; poor applicability in low-sweat or severe HF
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was founder/shareholder; another author was a Grace Imaging employee
tracking_note: Do not equate high correlation with interchangeability; sLT-VT analysis also reported fixed/proportional bias

title: Kinetic changes in sweat lactate following fatigue during constant workload exercise
exercise_context: constant-load cycling at 25% peak power; Test 1 to exhaustion then Test 2 for 10 min
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: pre- versus post-exhaustion sweat-lactate kinetics and subjective fatigue
key_result: post-fatigue curve shifted left; peak and 2/3/4 microampere points occurred sooner; all p<0.01
main_limitations: no a priori sample size; one load; young men only; incomplete nutrition/hydration control; chip replacement; no multimodal objective fatigue reference
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder and was not involved in data acquisition or analysis
tracking_note: Supports direction/timing change, not an absolute concentration cutoff

title: Constant Load Pedaling Exercise Combined with Electrical Muscle Stimulation Leads to an Early Increase in Sweat Lactate Levels
n_primary_analysis: 20 for sLT comparison; 15 completed 20 min in both conditions
exercise_context: 20-min constant-load cycling at 125% of premeasured VT with and without EMS
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: end-exercise blood lactate and EMS condition
key_result: sLT occurred earlier with EMS; between-condition sLT difference predicted end blood-lactate difference r=-0.52 p<0.05
fatigue_relevance: indirect; metabolic perturbation rather than fatigue validity
main_limitations: small all-male sample; completion attrition; apparently fixed condition order; incomplete prior-day exercise/fasting control
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder; paper states company had no involvement
tracking_note: Do not classify as direct fatigue-validation evidence

title: Implications of the Onset of Sweating on the Sweat Lactate Threshold
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: onset of sweating and blood lactate threshold
key_result: sLT-bLT r=0.68 overall; early-sweat group r=0.74; regular group r=0.61; five late-sweat cases had mean discrepancy 106.8 s
main_limitations: single exercise mode; observational; men only; late-sweat subgroup n=5
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder and was not involved in data acquisition or analysis
tracking_note: Sweat onset is not sLT but late sweat can delay sLT; implement a sweat-adequacy gate

title: Estimation of maximal lactate steady state using the sweat lactate sensor
population: adults with varied exercise habits; trained n=11 and untrained n=4
exercise_context: cycling for 30 min at 110/115/120/125% of sLT
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: blood-lactate-defined maximal lactate steady state and tissue oxygenation
key_result: individual MLSS was 110/115/120/125% of sLT in 1/4/3/7 participants; 80% trained >=120%; 75% untrained <=115%
fatigue_relevance: training prescription rather than fatigue diagnosis
main_limitations: very small sample; untrained n=4; group age/body-fat imbalance; no 130% test; observational
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was shareholder/CEO; Grace Imaging provided sensor equipment
tracking_note: No universal multiplier; stratify by training status and validate individually

title: Anaerobic threshold using sweat lactate sensor under hypoxia
population: healthy participants; article limitations describe college-aged men
exercise_context: incremental cycling in normoxia and hypoxia FiO2 15.4+/-0.8%
key_result: hypoxia sLT-VT r=0.70; intra-evaluator ICC=0.782; inter-evaluator ICC=0.933; mean difference -15.5 s
main_limitations: small selected sample; excluded low sweaters below 0.4 mg/cm2/min; one hypoxia level; current rather than calibrated concentration
tracking_note: Selection on sweat rate limits deployment generalizability

title: Lactate threshold evaluation in swimming using a sweat lactate sensor: A prospective study
exercise_context: incremental flume swimming with breaks for blood sampling and without breaks
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: blood lactate threshold speed and performance
key_result: sLT speed-bLT speed r=0.824; mean difference 0.08 m/s; no-break sLT versus break-test bLT r=0.868; some analyses showed fixed/proportional bias
main_limitations: single flume and water temperature; trained young swimmers; protocol breaks may alter threshold; environment affects sweating
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder and was not involved in data acquisition or analysis
tracking_note: Grace website text has DOI typo 10.10002; verified DOI is 10.1002/ejsc.12179

title: Sweat lactate sensor for detecting anaerobic threshold in heart failure: a prospective clinical trial (LacS-001)
population: heart failure NYHA class I-II; mostly men
design: prospective clinical trial; single-arm diagnostic agreement and safety
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: ventilatory threshold and device-related adverse events
key_result: sLT-VT r=0.651 95% CI 0.391-0.815; difference -4.9+/-15.0 W; 32/50 primary analysis; sLT interrater ICC=0.701; no device-related adverse event
fatigue_relevance: clinical threshold use; not direct fatigue monitoring
main_limitations: selected mild HF; primary analyzability 64%; limited women; no NYHA III; ergometer only; safety sample small
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was founder/shareholder; another author was founder/shareholder and sensor-chip patent holder
tracking_note: Report analyzability with accuracy; low/intermediate/high sweat groups had 53/100/75% clear sLT

title: A novel fatigue monitoring system using sweat lactate: a preliminary study
design: pre-match test-retest plus post-match observational study
exercise_context: incremental ergometer test; two pre-match and one 2 days post-match
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: ventilatory threshold and 10-Hz GNSS high-speed distance
key_result: sLT ICC=0.777 95% CI 0.506-0.910; sLT change correlated with high-speed distance r=0.64 and VT change r=0.77; study-protocol MDC95 about 10 W
main_limitations: small male college sample; one match and one post-match time point; ICC below 0.90; environmental/test-spacing effects; no hormonal/inflammatory/immune/enzymatic or neuromuscular comparator
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder and was not involved in data acquisition or analysis
tracking_note: Greater match high-speed distance tended to lower/earlier post-match sLT; retain both online and issue dates

title: Aerobic Threshold Evaluation Using a Sweat Lactate Sensor in Healthy Women
exercise_context: exercise test with respiratory gas analysis
key_result: sLT detected in all; sLT-VT Spearman r=0.769; sLT significantly delayed; sweat onset predicted discrepancy r=0.873
main_limitations: small healthy-women sample; systematic delay; full-text details not used because only abstract was accessible in this review
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder; company was not involved
tracking_note: Not listed on Grace official Paper page at verification date; abstract-level extraction only

title: Validation of aerobic threshold assessment using a sweat lactate sensor during arm crank exercise by healthy adults
population: healthy young adults; 9 men and 18 women
exercise_context: arm-crank ergometer; 5 W per min incremental protocol
key_result: sLT-VT1 workload r=0.904 and time r=0.859; mean differences 0.2 W and -7.7 s; no fixed or proportional bias
main_limitations: young healthy single-university sample; controlled environment; forehead only; 1-min stages; maximal aerobic capacity not formally assessed
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was president/shareholder; company was not involved
tracking_note: Grace website text has DOI typo 10.14814/phy2.17002; verified DOI is 10.14814/phy2.71002

title: Laminar flow ventilation system to prevent airborne infection during exercise in the COVID-19 crisis: A single-center observational study
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: respiratory particulate count and laminar-flow ventilation effect
key_result: sweat-lactate LT was used to segment exercise intensity; respiratory droplets rose after LT; LFVS reduced particles
main_limitations: small sample; primary endpoint was airborne particulate rather than sweat-lactate validity
conflict_of_interest: Nakashima was Grace Imaging shareholder/CEO; company provided lactate sensor equipment
tracking_note: Supporting application; do not count as a core sweat-lactate validation

title: Realtime Monitoring of Local Sweat Rate Kinetics during Constant-Load Exercise Using Perspiration-Meter with Airflow Compensation System
exercise_context: constant-load cycling at 25% peak power until exhaustion
key_result: two sweat-rate inflection points and time-varying forehead-to-arm relationship
main_limitations: small young male sample; no primary sweat-lactate endpoint; one exercise condition

title: Patient-centered medical tools for sustained motivation in cardiac rehabilitation of patients with heart failure: protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial (EXERCISE-HF trial)
design: multicenter open-label randomized controlled trial protocol
sensor_site: Fitbit wrist device; no sweat-lactate sensor endpoint
primary_comparator_or_endpoint: change in peak VO2 at 12 weeks; app versus standard care
main_limitations: no sweat-lactate measure/intervention/outcome; open label; protocol article
conflict_of_interest: Keio University and Grace Imaging disclosed financial interests/personal relationships
tracking_note: Excluded from sweat-lactate evidence synthesis despite appearance on Grace Paper page
